recent_articles.title: Assam inks settlement with Hmar, Kuki extremist groups - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article:
On Sunday, March 15, 2026, the **Assam** government signed a memorandum of settlement with three Kuki extremist groups and a Hmar group. The organizations involved are the **Hmar People’s Convention-Democratic (HPC-D)**, **United Kukigam Defence Army (UKDA)**, **Kuki Revolutionary Army (KRA)**, and the **Kuki Liberation Organisation (KLO)**, also known as the **Kuki Liberation Army**.  The groups had laid down their arms in 2012. The memorandum of settlement was signed in the presence of **Assam Education Minister Ranoj Pegu** and envisions the formation of a Hmar Welfare Development Council and a Kuki Welfare Development Council in Hmar and Kuki-dominated areas of Assam, respectively.  

The agreement followed a Suspension of Operations between the state government and these groups after they surrendered their arms. Tripartite talks involving the **Centre** led to the memorandum of settlement, which was accelerated in recent months as an initiative for peace and tranquillity in the state and to fulfill the aspirations of both communities. The councils will be headquartered in Guwahati and their budgets will be prepared according to their needs submitted to the **Transformation and Development Department**. 

The government also pledged to take appropriate measures to rehabilitate the cadres of the armed groups, including compensation for family members of those who lost their lives during their struggle.  **Assam** claims that this memorandum of settlement has brought the ethnic militancy issue in Assam to an end, adding that over 9,000 cadres from various extremist groups, including those from the Bodo, Karbi and Adivasi communities, have been rehabilitated in recent years. These groups have also deposited 1,012 firearms, 25,488 rounds of ammunition, and 34 grenades.
